entries.a: Hello! I'm Preet's site assistant. Ask me anything about his work, skills, projects, teaching, or how to reach him.

Preet Mehta is a Data Engineer working as Manager, Healthcare Analytics at EXL Service in New York. He has about 10 years of experience in data engineering and data architecture, with the last 6 years deep in healthcare — building pipelines, modern data platforms, and ML systems. He's also a teacher and mentor: he's guided around 3,000 students one-on-one and runs a 1,500-member WhatsApp community where he teaches data engineering.

Preet is Manager, Healthcare Analytics at EXL Service in New York. He leads a team building healthcare analytics platforms — solution architecture, data pipelines, data governance, and ML models. Two of his flagship builds there: a nephrology RCM (revenue cycle management) data platform, and a Medicaid churn prediction model with roughly $300M in business impact.

About 10 years across data engineering, data architecture, and big-data solutions — including 6 years in healthcare. He started working with data in a project-management role before doing his master's, and has been a full-time data engineer for around 8 years.
Preet interned as a Data Engineer at LinkedIn in New York (2022, 8 months), building ETL pipelines on Hadoop/Presto/Azkaban and reporting for Talent Solutions and sales operations.

At CVS Health (about 1.8 years), Preet worked in analytics and behavior-change programs — including data pipelines behind campaigns reaching 340M members, daily ingestion with Airflow, and marketing platforms like Marketo and Adobe Experience Platform.
At Searce, Preet was a Looker consultant and developer — he got Looker-certified in 30 days and delivered BI solutions across multiple clients on Google Cloud.
Early in his career at DCM Shriram, Preet worked with plant-machine IoT data and supply-chain analytics, plus PMO dashboards.
One of Preet's biggest wins: a Medicaid churn prediction model at EXL with roughly $300M in business impact — identifying members likely to churn so the business could act in time.
At CVS Health, Preet built data pipelines behind member campaigns reaching 340 million members — daily ingestion with Airflow feeding marketing platforms.
Preet leads a team of 4 building a Medicare Stars ML model at EXL (for Humana) — predicting star-rating measures that directly affect plan revenue and member care quality.

Preet's core stack: Python, SQL, Apache Spark / PySpark, Databricks, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Azure Data Factory, SQL Server, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker, Tableau, plus data modeling, ETL/ELT, data governance, and machine learning. He's cloud-agnostic and problem-first. You can click any skill in the periodic table on this site to see the projects where he actually used it.

Yes — Python is Preet's primary language for pipelines, transformations, and ML feature work. His GitHub repos (Russian Troll Tweets analysis, wildfire prediction, flight-fare prediction) are all Python.
Yes — Apache Spark / PySpark is one of Preet's core tools for large-scale batch processing. He's also spoken about Spark at the NYC meetup.
Yes — Databricks (Delta Lake, Unity Catalog) is central to Preet's lakehouse work. He's also the official organizer of the Boston Databricks User Group.
Yes — SQL is foundational to everything Preet builds: warehouses, marts, and analytics across SQL Server and BigQuery.

Yes — Preet builds ML systems, not just pipelines: the ~$300M Medicaid churn model, a Medicare Stars model, and an Alzheimer's biomarker research project with Stanford using ADNI data. He also has several ML projects on GitHub (wildfire prediction, flight-fare prediction, sentiment analysis).

Preet is cloud-agnostic: Azure (Data Factory), Google Cloud (BigQuery, Looker), and he's renewing his Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer certification. He picks the platform that fits the problem.

Yes — across all three: Power BI (he won a DAESO hackathon with it), Tableau (several public dashboards: OTT subscribers, Spotify, Game of Thrones), and Looker (certified LookML developer and former consultant).
Healthcare data is Preet's deepest domain (6 years): claims data, EMR/clinical feeds, HEDIS quality measures, and HCC risk adjustment — across CVS Health and EXL's payer/provider work.

Preet has a master's from Northeastern University (2023), where he was also a Teaching Assistant. Before that, he did his bachelor's in mechanical engineering in India and spent ~4 years in project management at a chemical manufacturing company — that's where he first fell in love with data.
Preet won the Feretti & Yamamura Award for Best Teaching Assistant (2023) at Northeastern, and has about 4 company awards from EXL. See the Achievements section for the full list.
Teaching is Preet's passion: he's mentored around 3,000 students one-on-one, was a TA at Northeastern, and runs a 1,500-member WhatsApp community with regular teaching sessions on data engineering.

Preet has designed and judged hackathons at Northeastern about 9 times, and judges events like HackUMass and UBHacking. He's actively building a profile as a judge and mentor at data engineering conferences.

Preet has spoken at UMass Amherst (keynote), the Apache Spark meetup in NYC, and was an industry panelist at UMass Amherst's 'Future of Computing' tech conference alongside Google, NVIDIA, and MathWorks panelists.
Preet is the official organizer of the Boston Databricks User Group — he runs the chapter, lines up speakers, and is planning sponsored in-person events.

Preet writes 30+ articles on data engineering — daily on Substack ('Healthcare for Data Engineers' / masterdataengineering.substack.com) and on Medium. This site has a writing hub pulling his latest posts.

Preet has 18 personal projects in this site's archive — data visualizations (Tableau, Data Studio), machine learning (wildfire prediction, flight-fare prediction, sentiment analysis), and data engineering (a Yelp data warehouse, an e-commerce OLTP design). Scroll to Personal Projects, or click any skill in the periodic table to see where he used it.
His 'Data Warehouse for Yelp' project designs a full warehouse on the Yelp dataset — modeling, ETL, and analytics-ready marts. It's on his GitHub (ynpreet).
'Flight Fare Prediction' is an ML web app Preet built and deployed — predicting airfares with a trained model behind a live app. On his GitHub (ynpreet).
The best way to reach Preet is LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/preetmehta. He also shares daily data-engineering content on Substack and Medium (links in the Contact section).
Preet's GitHub is github.com/ynpreet — ML projects, data warehouses, and ETL work, all public.
Preet is based in Boston, Massachusetts.

Preet is open to judging hackathons and competitions, mentoring, speaking engagements, workshops, and research collaborations (he contributes data-engineering expertise to research papers). Reach him on LinkedIn.
You're welcome! Anything else you'd like to know about Preet?
